transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel, Samira O'Neill (Redwood); Carlos Mendez, Priya Suresh, Oliver Kim (Fairwind)

Summary (auto): initial security posture discovery to evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Key topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency and retention. Next steps agreed: share certs and architecture, schedule deep dive.

Topics: security posture, compliance docs, key management, VPC/private deployment, retention policy

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We've got Samira here from our security/solutions engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Carlos Mendez: Good afternoon. Thanks, Jordan. Carlos here, CISO at Fairwind. We wanted to run through Redwood's security posture; where credit card and sensitive investor data might touch things, etc.
[00:15] Priya Suresh: Hi, Priya. Platform lead. We're primarily evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for inference. Main concerns are encryption, KMS integration, auditability, and how SSO works.
[00:25] Samira O'Neill: Great, thanks. We'll cover SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS, and data retention. Also happy to talk about network options — VPC/Private and on-prem if needed.
[00:35] Oliver Kim: Quick note: our infra team is sensitive to multitenancy — we prefer dedicated capacity if there's no heavy lift. But cost is a consideration.

[02:10] Jordan Patel: To frame it — Hosted is easiest to start, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with isolation, and Private is full customer-managed. A lot of customers start hosted, then move to Dedicated or Private as they scale or hit compliance.
[02:28] Carlos Mendez: For us, the question is data in flight and at rest: who has access, where keys live, and retention policies. Do you have SOC2 and ISO certificates?
[02:40] Samira O'Neill: Yes — we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. I'll share the certs and our most recent pen test report after the call. Note: hosted environment is Redwood-managed, certs cover our production control plane and hosted API.
[03:05] Priya Suresh: Does your SOC2 scope include hosted inference logs and model outputs or just control plane?
[03:12] Samira O'Neill: Good Q. The scope covers both control plane and production inference service for our hosted product — including logging & change controls. For Dedicated and Private, scope differs depending on managed services vs customer-managed; we provide guidance and we can include elements in attestation for managed Dedicated contracts.

[05:00] Oliver Kim: On KMS — we use HashiCorp Vault in-house and AWS KMS for some workloads. We require that keys for customer data stay in our KMS. Is that supported?
[05:10] Samira O'Neill: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS. We integrate with AWS KMS and provide HSM/KMS integration patterns; with Private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS and keys never leave your VPC/HSM. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption — keys at rest are managed by Redwood but we do offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for enterprise customers via a dedicated contract — there may be additional compliance steps.
[05:45] Carlos Mendez: Can you clarify BYOK for Hosted? Does Redwood have access to plaintext in memory on the inference nodes?
[05:53] Samira O'Neill: In all cases inference uses plaintext in memory during inference — that's inherent to compute. Our controls are around who can access the compute hosts, key rotation, and audit logs. For highest assurance customers we recommend Dedicated / Private where keys are customer controlled and network isolation prevents Redwood ops from reaching the inference hosts unless explicitly enabled for support.

[07:30] Priya Suresh: Audit logs — do you provide immutable logs and can they be exported to our SIEM? We need logs for model inputs, admin access, and configuration changes.
[07:42] Jordan Patel: Yes, we provide audit logs. For Hosted we have tenant-level logs and can forward logs to customer SIEM via a secure delivery channel (S3 or syslog). For Dedicated/Private you control log aggregation; we can also ship agents or provide a connector. We keep logs for X days by default — what's your retention requirement?
[08:05] Carlos Mendez: We're governed to keep certain access logs for 7 years for compliance — although some data is redacted depending on sensitivity. But we want an exportable audit trail.
[08:15] Samira O'Neill: Seven years is long. For Hosted we typically retain production audit logs for 365 days in our standard package; extended retention is an add-on. For Dedicated and Private you can set retention according to your policy — as long as the storage is provisioned. We'll include retention options in the follow-up.

[10:00] Oliver Kim: RBAC — we need role separation and least privilege. Can you map to our existing roles from SSO?
[10:08] Samira O'Neill: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC and map external groups to internal roles. We have fine-grained RBAC: admins, billing, deploy, read-only, etc. For Dedicated/Private you can also integrate with your IdP for automated provisioning.
[10:30] Priya Suresh: Does SAML just work for Hosted? Any differences?
[10:35] Jordan Patel: Functionally it's the same — Hosted supports SAML/OIDC, just provisioning/back-channel differs. For Dedicated/Private you have more control on network-level SAML endpoints.

[12:00] Carlos Mendez: Encryption at rest — do you encrypt model artifacts and cache? Also are KV caches encrypted?
[12:10] Samira O'Neill: Yes, at rest we encrypt disks and model artifacts. KV cache can be encrypted with customer keys in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we encrypt with our keys but we have envelope encryption support for enterprise.
[12:35] Oliver Kim: For the model weights — some customers want to ensure models are pinned and not auto-updated. Is that possible?
[12:42] Samira O'Neill: Absolutely. You can pin model versions and we support rollout policies. That's part of our deployment abstraction so you control which model builds are used in inference.

[15:00] Priya Suresh: Data residency — we have EU-resident investor data. Do you offer regionally isolated hosted endpoints?
[15:08] Jordan Patel: Yes — our hosted API has regional endpoints and our enterprise contracts can guarantee region-local processing; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in-region or Private (VPC/On-prem).

[17:00] Carlos Mendez: Pen test — do you do external pentests and will you share the report?
[17:06] Samira O'Neill: We commission third-party pen tests annually. We'll share the executive summary and redacted reports under an NDA. Full raw reports have limited distribution.

[20:00] Oliver Kim: SLA and support — in Dedicated can we get access to run our own scanning tools against the hosts?
[20:10] Jordan Patel: For Dedicated we have defined support windows and can agree to scanning windows. For Private/on-prem you have full access. For Hosted we'd need to coordinate. We'll document scanning guidelines in the follow-up.

[22:30] Priya Suresh: Regarding logs again — can we get model input/output logs if we request? Some of that is sensitive.
[22:40] Samira O'Neill: We do capture request/response metadata for debugging; storing raw outputs is configurable. For Hosted, retention and raw output capture are configurable per contract. For privacy we offer input/output redaction and differential logging. We'll detail options in writing.

[25:00] Carlos Mendez: How about encryption keys — rotation and audit? Can we rotate keys without downtime?
[25:08] Samira O'Neill: We support key rotation with minimal impact through envelope keys and rolling re-encryption strategies. For Dedicated/Private with customer-managed KMS you control rotation cadence; our runtime handles rotated keys transparently. We'll include operational notes.

[28:00] Oliver Kim: Does Redwood provide HSM integrations for FIPS requirements?
[28:06] Samira O'Neill: Yes, HSM-backed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have HSM controls in our cloud provider chain; enterprise customers can contract for HSM-backed key management.

[30:00] Priya Suresh: Any compliance artifacts for SOC2 we should expect to see? Policies, control narratives, evidence collection procedures?
[30:08] Samira O'Neill: We'll send the SOC 2 Type II cert and a control summary. For customers doing vendor risk we also provide an ISMS overview, change management docs, and a list of controls mapped to common questionnaires (SIG, etc.).

[33:00] Carlos Mendez: Network isolation — can Dedicated be deployed in a single-tenant VPC owned by us?
[33:10] Samira O'Neill: Dedicated means reserved capacity; network topology can be configured. For high compliance, Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) places control with you. We offer VPC peering and private connectivity options.

[35:30] Jordan Patel: Quick cost tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest but less isolated; Dedicated gives isolation with predictable throughput and SLA; Private gives max control but is most ops-heavy. Which direction is Fairwind leaning?
[35:45] Carlos Mendez: Probable path is start with Hosted for eval (if data can be redacted) then pilot Dedicated in-region with BYOK and extended retention. If that doesn't meet requirements, move to Private.

[38:00] Priya Suresh: Can you provide an example architecture for Dedicated with BYOK and log forwarding? We'd like a diagram and configuration steps.
[38:10] Samira O'Neill: Yes — I'll include an architecture diagram showing KMS in customer account, VPC peering, audit log forwarding to S3/SIEM, and support connectors.

[40:00] Oliver Kim: Any open issues you commonly see in onboarding security reviews?
[40:05] Samira O'Neill: Common items: clarity on key ownership, retention windows, cross-region replication, and support access policies. We'll include recommended language you can use in your vendor risk management.

[42:00] Jordan Patel: Recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO certs and redacted pen test, share Dedicated/Private architecture diagrams, include BYOK/KMS integration notes, and propose dates for a technical deep dive.
[42:15] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. We'll pull together KMS vendor info and retention policy and meet again after we review.
[42:25] Priya Suresh: Week of July 5th works for a deep dive.
[42:30] Jordan Patel: Great — action items and owners in the notes. Thanks everyone.
[42:36] Carlos Mendez: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
